title: Notice of termination by the employer during a protected period (CO art. 336c)

sources.title: Swiss Code of Obligations (SR 220), consolidated version of 2026-10-01 (Fedlex); English translation, German text authoritative

facts.question: Which employment-termination dispute does the claim concern: notice during a protected period, wrongful (abusive) notice, or dismissal with immediate effect?
Did the employer give the employee notice of termination of the employment relationship?
Was the notice given after the probation period had expired?
Does the file say that a written individual agreement, a standard employment contract or a collective employment contract set a probation period other than the first month of employment?
Was the employee, through no fault of their own, wholly or partly prevented from working by illness or accident on the day notice was given or while the notice period was still running?

Was the employee performing Swiss compulsory military service, civil defence service or alternative civilian service on the day notice was given or while the notice period was running, or, for such a service lasting more than eleven days, did either of those fall within the four weeks before or after it?
Was the employee pregnant, or within sixteen weeks after giving birth, on the day notice was given or while the notice period was running?
Was the notice given before the protected period began, with the notice period not yet expired when it began?

Does the file say that a written individual employment contract, a standard employment contract or a collective employment contract sets notice periods different from the statutory ones (one month in the first year of service, two months in the second to ninth years, three months thereafter)?

documents.title: Notice of termination
documents.why: CO art. 336c para. 2: Voidness turns on the day the notice was given compared with the protected period; the notice and its date of receipt are the ordinary record of that day.

documents.title: Employment contract or other record of the start of employment
documents.why: CO art. 335b para. 1: The probation period, and with it the start of the protection, runs from the start of employment; the contract or another record of the start date ordinarily shows it.

documents.title: Written probation clause (individual agreement, standard or collective contract)
must_show: the written instrument that sets it
documents.why: CO art. 335b para. 2: A probation period other than the first month exists only under a written agreement or a standard or collective contract; that written clause proves its length and so whether notice came after it.

documents.title: Medical certificate of incapacity for work
must_show: first and last day of incapacity
documents.why: CO art. 336c para. 1 let. b: The bar applies only while the employee is prevented from working by illness or accident; a medical certificate is the ordinary proof of that incapacity and its dates, to compare with the notice.

documents.title: Official confirmation of compulsory service
must_show: kind of service (military, civil defence, alternative civilian)
first and last day of service
documents.why: CO art. 336c para. 1 let. a: The bar depends on the kind of service, its dates and whether it lasted more than eleven days; the official service order or confirmation ordinarily shows all three.

documents.title: Medical confirmation of pregnancy or record of the birth
must_show: pregnancy confirmed and its dates, or the date of birth
documents.why: CO art. 336c para. 1 let. c: The bar runs during pregnancy and sixteen weeks after the birth; a medical confirmation of the pregnancy or the birth record ordinarily dates that period.

documents.title: Written notice-period clause (individual, standard or collective contract)
must_show: end-point of the notice (e.g. end of a month)
the written instrument that sets it (individual, standard or collective contract)
documents.why: CO art. 336c para. 3: Resuming and extending a suspended notice period needs its length and end-point; where a written contract varies the statutory periods, that clause is the ordinary proof of them.

steps.title: Establish whether the employer gave notice
Check that the probation period had expired when notice was given
Record the notice, the start of employment and the probation terms
Examine the illness or accident protected period
Examine the pregnancy and maternity protected period
Compute the suspended and extended notice period
Check whether the notice fell inside a protected period and is void
Assess the effect of the notice (void, suspended or valid)
Check branch: notice before the protected period
Record the document state for assessment

outcomes.title: Process ends: The provision restrains only a termination by the employer
Process ends: The bar applies only after the probation period has expired

presumptions.text: CO art. 335b para. 1: “the probation period is considered to be the first month of an employment relationship” The statute deems the probation period to be the first month and paragraph 2 allows other terms only in writing, so where the file states no such written term the first month applies.

CO art. 335c para. 1: “The employment relationship may be terminated at one month’s notice during the first year of service, at two months’ notice in the second to ninth years of service and at three months’ notice thereafter, all such notice to expire at the end of a calendar month.” Paragraph 1 fixes the notice periods by law and paragraph 2 lets them differ only by a written individual, standard or collective contract, so where the file states no such written term the statutory periods apply.

notes.text: No public text in this rule set supports presuming an unmentioned branch fact absent or the defining event present; such a fact stays unresolved and documents that depend on it are held behind its question. Only the statutory defaults listed under presumptions apply.
